sentences.text: Did you measure the drop from your skimmer to the waterfall, or are we guessing on head height again? Prices climb sharply once a koi passes the twenty-inch mark — growth potential is proven, not promised. Check valve, ball valve, three-way — which fitting failed on you this time? "Cut feeding to once a day when the water hits sixty," she told him, tapping the tub of wheat-germ pellets. If your pond drops below eighteen inches deep, ice can lock it solid, and the fish have nowhere to hold over. Nobody warns you that a half-finished pond in July becomes a mosquito nursery by August. We recommend a bottom drain on anything over two thousand gallons; vacuuming a liner pond by hand gets old fast. Grading happens every Thursday morning: body conformation first, then skin luster, then pattern edges under the north-facing skylight. The 45-mil EPDM liner comes in twenty-foot rolls, and we cut it right off the spool while you wait. What eats a pond's oxygen fastest isn't the fish; it's the rotting leaves you never netted out in November. A customer once sketched his whole backyard on the back of a receipt while I priced out underlayment by the square foot. Underlayment goes down first, then liner, then a ring of flat fieldstone to hide the folded edges. She picked out a butterfly koi with trailing fins the color of weak tea, then asked whether raccoons would eat it. Never lift a showa bare-handed; wet the sock net first or you'll scrape the mucus coat clean off. Twelve dollars a foot for the flexible PVC, and honestly, the rigid stuff fights you around every curve. By late October the yard smells of wet rubber and cedar shavings, and every pallet holds netting for leaf season. Winterizing kit, aisle three — de-icer, aerator stone, and the cold-water bacteria that keep working below fifty degrees. The kohaku in bay six, the one with the stepped hi pattern? Sold this morning to a collector from Dayton. Last spring we replaced eleven burst check valves for customers who skipped draining their external plumbing before the freeze. Our pumps are rated in gallons per hour at zero head, so knock off roughly ten percent for every vertical foot. What is the meaning of the word tank?
